cases.reason: A fold removes the CRLF *and* the whitespace after it -- all three characters. A binding removing only the CRLF yields 'Hello World', silently inserting a space into the user's text at every fold point.
HTAB is a fold character too, not just SPACE. Caught by 0 of the other §2 cases -- every one of them uses SPACE, so a binding matching /\r\n /  alone passes them all.

§2 is two steps and this pins their composition: step 1 rewrites a bare LF to CRLF, so step 2 then sees a fold. A binding that unfolds on CRLF without normalising first passes every CRLF case here and fails this one -- and LF-only ICS is what real calendar servers emit.

A lone CR is not a line ending, so step 1 leaves it and step 2 never matches: the CR and the space both survive into the value. The mirror image of the LF case -- together they pin exactly which endings normalise and which do not.
An LF-only document with no fold in it at all, so step 1 is exercised on its own. Rejecting LF-only ICS would fail documents every other client reads.
Two folds in one logical line. A binding whose replacement is not global, or which rescans from the wrong offset, joins two of the three segments and drops the third.
Property names are case-insensitive, and §3.1 requires uppercasing rather than a case-insensitive comparison, because the uppercased form is what §5.2's table is keyed by.

A line with no colon at all: the name is the whole line and the value is empty. Pinned on SUMMARY so the result is observable -- summary becomes the empty string, not an absence. On an unknown name the rule would be untestable, since both readings ignore the line.

§3.1's two sentences are in tension and the second one wins: with no colon anywhere, the name is the ENTIRE line, semicolon and all, so this selects no member and SUMMARY stays an absence. Reading only the first sentence -- 'before the first ; or :' -- gives the name SUMMARY and an empty-string summary instead. Caught by 0 of the 58 cases that existed before it: its sibling name-line-with-no-colon carries no semicolon, so both readings agree on it. Found by review of the Python binding, where a reviewer proposed exactly the losing reading.

The name ends at the first ';' or ':' *whichever comes first*. Here the ';' is inside the value, so it must not shorten the name. A binding splitting on ';' unconditionally produces the name 'SUMMARY:A' and drops the property.
The value is everything after the first colon, so a value containing further colons keeps them. A binding splitting on every colon truncates every URL.

Divergence #1 in §9, pinned rather than fixed. RFC 5545 permits a colon inside a double-quoted parameter value; §3.2 takes the first colon unconditionally, so the value here begins mid-parameter. A binding implementing quoted-parameter awareness returns 'actual' and does not conform.
The VALUE=DATE parameter on DTSTART sets allDay.

Whole-element matching is load-bearing: a substring test makes VALUE=DATE match VALUE=DATE-TIME and turns every timed event into an all-day one. Caught by 0 of the other cases -- no other case carries a parameter that merely starts with VALUE=DATE.
A ';' after the first ':' is inside the value, so there are no parameters at all. A binding scanning the whole line for 'VALUE=DATE' reads one out of the value and sets allDay on a timed event.
Backslash is escaped first, so a literal backslash in the value becomes exactly two. Any other ordering re-escapes a backslash this function itself emitted.
Steps 2 and 3: ';' and ',' are escaped in TEXT values.
Step 4 folds both CRLF and a bare LF to the two-character escape. A binding matching only CRLF leaves a raw newline in the value, which breaks the line structure of the document it is building.
A colon is not escaped: RFC 5545 does not require it in a TEXT value, and §3.2 splits on the first colon, which is always the property's own separator in a line this function builds.

THE single-pass proof. The wire value is backslash, backslash, 'n' -- three characters -- and must yield the TWO characters backslash and 'n', NOT a newline. A '\\'->'\' pass followed by a '\n'->newline pass collapses it to a newline instead, at any ordering. Only a single left-to-right pass that consumes the escaped character is correct.
Both '\n' and '\N' map to U+000A. Deliberately lenient: this reads documents the library did not write.
Unescaping accepts escapes escaping does not produce: '\q' yields 'q'. A binding rejecting or preserving an unknown escape does not conform.
A backslash that is the last character has nothing to consume, so it is emitted as itself. A binding indexing past the end here reads undefined or raises.
VCALENDAR headers and a VTIMEZONE component sit outside any VEVENT block and are discarded. This is how §9 divergence 4 -- only VEVENT is read -- is realised.
A BEGIN:VEVENT with no matching END:VEVENT is discarded, not emitted. A binding that flushes whatever it accumulated at end of input returns a truncated event.
Two blocks yield two events, in document order -- a master plus a RECURRENCE-ID override is the shape this exists for.

A second BEGIN:VEVENT opens a block and discards anything accumulated, so the first UID never reaches an event. A binding treating BEGIN as a no-op inside a block emits one event with the FIRST uid, since §5.2's last-wins would not apply across the reset.
A line's UPPERCASED form is compared to BEGIN:VEVENT and END:VEVENT, so lowercase markers open and close a block.
One block exercising every row of §5.2's table at once, so a binding that silently drops a member fails here rather than only in whichever single-member case happens to cover it.
An unrecognised name is ignored: not an error, and not retained anywhere.

Leading and trailing whitespace in a SUMMARY is part of the text the user typed. A binding trimming all seven trimmed properties plus the three text ones -- the obvious uniform implementation -- fails here.
Whitespace around a UID is noise. The mirror of the SUMMARY case: together they pin the trimmed/not-trimmed split as deliberate rather than incidental.
A repeated property keeps the last occurrence.

allDay is recomputed per DTSTART line, so it reflects the LAST one only. A binding OR-ing allDay across occurrences -- the natural way to write it if allDay is set only when the parameter is present -- reports true here.

§R7's set includes U+FEFF. Python's str.strip() and Go's strings.TrimSpace do NOT strip it, so a binding delegating to its host trim returns the BOM followed by 'abc'. Catches a delegating Python and a delegating Go.

§R7's set EXCLUDES U+001C. Python's str.strip() strips it, so a delegating Python binding returns 'abc' where the specification requires the separator to survive. The mirror of the U+FEFF case -- they fail in opposite directions and neither implies the other.

A supplied-but-empty SUMMARY is the empty string, which §1 distinguishes from the absence a block with no SUMMARY produces. In Go this is what forces *string over §R6's zero value: a zero-valued string cannot tell these two apart.
The organizer is everything after the first mailto:, trimmed.
The search is case-insensitive, so an uppercase MAILTO: is found.

THE case this corpus exists for. U+0130 is the one code point whose full lowercase is LONGER than itself, so a binding that searches value.toLowerCase() and then slices the ORIGINAL at the index it found is off by one from here on: TypeScript and Python both return 'ane@example.com', and Go -- whose simple case mapping SHRINKS U+0130 -- returns ':jane@example.com'. Three bindings, two wrong answers, none correct. §5.3's ASCII-only fold is what makes the index valid in the original under all three languages' indexing rules. The U+0130 is in PREFIX TEXT, which §5.3 explicitly tolerates, so this case does not depend on §3.2's divergence and keeps biting if divergence #1 is ever corrected. Caught by 0 of the 29 unit tests that existed before it.

The same defect reached the way a real document would reach it: RFC 5545 permits a colon inside a quoted parameter value, so §3.2 splits INSIDE the quotes and the rest of the parameter -- U+0130 and all -- lands in the value ahead of the mailto:. This is §3.2's divergence #1 composing with §5.3. Its sibling case pins the same rule without depending on that divergence. Note an ordinary CN=Istanbul parameter with no quoted colon does NOT reach the defect: §3.2 removes the whole parameter section along with the first colon, so the U+0130 never enters the value.
A value with no mailto: yields an absence, and organizer is set to it.

'mailto:' with nothing after it yields the empty string, which §5.3 distinguishes from the absence of the previous case -- organizer takes the extraction result including an empty one. The ATTENDEE rule is the opposite, which is the next case.

An ATTENDEE is appended only when the extraction produced a NON-EMPTY string, so the same input that gives organizer '' contributes no attendee. A binding sharing one code path between the two members fails one of these two cases whichever way it chooses.
attendees never contains an absence.
ATTENDEE accumulates in document order, unlike every other repeated property, which keeps the last. A binding sorting or reversing fails here.
An event with no UID cannot be correlated with an update or a cancellation, so the block is dropped and everything parsed from it discarded with it.
A UID that is empty after trimming drops the block, and -- the half that matters -- parsing continues with the next block. A binding returning early on a dropped block loses every later event.
A failure spanning the whole document yields an empty list, never an error (§R6).
An END:VEVENT with no open block, and content between blocks, are both tolerated: malformed input produces fewer events, never an error.
The eleven-line minimal document, pinned byte for byte per §R5 -- including the absence of PRODID, which RFC 5545 §3.6 requires and §9 item 3 records as a scope decision.
Lines 9 and 10 appear, in that order, after SUMMARY and before any ATTENDEE.

Presence is tested, not truthiness: a supplied-but-empty description still emits 'DESCRIPTION:' with an empty value. A binding testing for a non-empty string omits the line and does not conform. Caught by 0 of the other build cases -- every other one supplies a non-empty description or none at all.
An empty attendees list contributes no lines, and is indistinguishable in the output from attendees being omitted -- which build-minimal is. The pair pins that.
One ATTENDEE line per address, in the order given.

Only lines 8, 9 and 10 are escaped. uid, now, start, end and each attendee address are interpolated RAW, so a semicolon in the uid survives unescaped. A binding escaping uniformly emits 'UID:u\;1' and does not conform.
Every line is terminated by CRLF including the last, so the returned string ends with CRLF. A binding joining on CRLF without appending one produces a document whose final line is unterminated.

Settled by RFC-0018: a content line of any length is emitted whole. This SUMMARY line is well over 75 octets and the expected output contains no CRLF-plus-whitespace sequence anywhere, so a binding that started folding fails here. Together with the multibyte case this is what makes §7 executable rather than merely provisional.

The same claim where octet length and character length disagree: these are three-octet characters, so octet 75 falls mid-character. Under RFC-0018 there is no fold, so the line is emitted whole; §7.1's alignment rule is what would govern if a future revision added one, and remains unenforceable while §7 stands.
